page: Microsoft Azure D4d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance is provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical processor cores via multithreading. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, complemented by 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. The host platform supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, along with hardware-assisted cryptographic primitives like AES-NI and SHA-NI.

Unlike diskless D-series configurations, the D4d_v5 includes 161 GB of temporary local solid-state storage directly attached to the host, facilitating low-latency scratch space and temporary file operations without incurring network disk overhead. The server does not incorporate hardware GPU accelerators and is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking or separate IP allocations.

Empirical benchmarks reveal mid-tier single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to its 2 physical core limit. Geekbench reports a single-core score of 1566.0, situated within the middle 50% of tested instances, whereas the multi-core result reaches 3357.0, ranking in the lower quartile. Similarly, stress-ng shows moderate single-core throughput at 1896.79 points alongside a multi-core score of 3867.66. Memory bandwidth tests yield 29.03 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 24.04 GB/sec for writes. Workloads requiring intensive multi-threading or heavy memory subsystem performance, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (18.68 GB/sec) and PassMark database operations (1670.03), land in lower performance tiers.

Cost efficiency is anchored by the balanced memory ratio and the inclusion of local temporary SSD capacity, which eliminates the baseline spend on external storage for ephemeral operational data. However, the throughput constraints on concurrent computing limit its suitability for large parallel builds or high-concurrency ingestion pipelines. The instance is best suited for balanced enterprise workloads, mid-scale web applications, caching tiers, development environments, and batch processing tasks requiring local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage, it provides a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory profile without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments position its single-thread execution in the middle 50% range, achieving 1566.0 in Geekbench and 1896.79 in stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core operations and memory subsystem tests fall into lower performance brackets due to the physical core limitation, with memory read bandwidth reaching 29.03 GB/sec and Redis throughput measuring 3.88 million operations per second. The instance delivers balanced resource allocation and integrated ephemeral storage for general enterprise tasks, lightweight web hosting, intermediate caching, and microservices.
